conventions.convention: Column vectorization stacks columns; the Sylvester matrix is I_n ⊗ A + B^T ⊗ I_m, using transpose rather than adjoint even over C.
sep(A,-B) measures X ↦ AX+XB in Frobenius norm; its second argument includes a conventional minus sign. Matrix dimensions m,n are positive.
Hurwitz means strictly negative real parts of all complex eigenvalues. The Lyapunov equation is AX+XA*+Q=0, with self-adjoint Q; star means transpose over R and conjugate transpose over C.

ADI uses negative-real-part shifts, c_j=-2 Re(p_j), and R_j=R_{j-1}+c_j V_j. Real-data nonreal shifts are validated in consecutive conjugate pairs, but updates process each individual shift and may use complex arithmetic.

Bartels–Stewart accepts computed Schur factors only after exact certificate checks. Block columns increase and block rows decrease. A nonzero determinant is rejected when its certified separation lower bound is at most the threshold, including equality.

The cubic Bartels–Stewart bound counts exact integer/rational operations as scalar operations, assumes linearly bounded sweep budgets and dimension-independent controller budgets, and makes no bit-complexity claim.

load_bearing.statement: For F∈{R,C}, m,n≥1 and compatible square A,B, the Sylvester map is invertible if and only if σ(A)∩(-σ(B))=∅, with real spectra taken over C. This is equivalent to unique solvability for every right-hand side and to sep(A,-B)>0.

Finite-budget Schur calls produce candidates; exact Schur certificates precede block substitution. Each local Kronecker matrix must have nonzero determinant and δ(M)>τ before its adjugate solve is stored. Successful completion returns X=UYV* and its exact residual.

For admitted inputs the procedure terminates with a declared status; every stored local solve is unique. On success the full equation has exactly one solution, without an additional spectral-disjointness assumption, because successful local pivot checks imply invertibility of the full block operator.

For Hurwitz A and self-adjoint Q, the integral of e^{tA}Qe^{tA*} over [0,∞) converges and uniquely solves AX+XA*+Q=0. Nonnegative Q gives nonnegative X; positive Q gives positive X. For nonnegative Q, X is positive exactly when no nonzero trajectory e^{tA*}v remains in ker Q^{1/2} for every t≥0.
For every completed ADI iterate j, with X_0=0 and R_0=B, AX_j+X_jA*+BB*=R_jR_j*.
For Hurwitz A with unitary Schur form T=D+N and α=-max Re σ(A)>0, ||e^{tA}||₂≤e^{-αt} Σ_{k=0}^{n-1}(t||N||₂)^k/k! for every t≥0.
For the unique solution X and any approximation X̂, if R=C-(AX̂+X̂B) and sep(A,-B)>0, then ||X-X̂||_F≤||R||_F/sep(A,-B).

concerns.concern: Step 3.1 writes: “If R_j=UΣV* is an SVD, then R_jR_j*=UΣ²U*”. Here R_j has shape n×r and r need not equal n, so the full SVD factor Σ is rectangular and Σ² is undefined. The required product is ΣΣ*, whose diagonal contains the squared singular values. The following norm inequality is correct and closes immediately with that product.

seams_checked.note: Checked the actual Schur procedure, real/complex Schur definitions, exact discriminant predicate and rational sign recipe, finite-status theorem, and supporting chase/similarity descriptions against Bartels–Stewart and its property proofs. Computed Schur output remains a candidate; exact factorization is checked separately. Finite controls and evaluator cost qualifications are preserved.

Checked the principal square-root uniqueness proof, Schur–Parlett algorithm and correctness proof, and finite-algorithm termination theorem. The spectral Sylvester criterion is used with opposite half-planes. Schur–Parlett obtains uniqueness from successful local pivots through the explicit finite-status/local-pivot theorem, rather than assuming an unverified spectral premise. Exact-certificate and failure-status qualifications are retained.
